title: History | Volkswagen Newsroom
content: The history of the Volkswagen brand began with the “Käfer”; development work on this Nazi prestige project began in 1934. With the Type 1 (Käfer) model, and the Type 2 (Transporter) model added in 1950, Volkswagen became a symbol of Germany’s economic miracle, above all as a result of the strong export orientation on the part of the company converted into a joint stock corporation in 1960. Innovative and flexible manufacturing systems made an appearance in the 1970s and led to the birth of a new generation of Volkswagens with the Passat, Scirocco, Golf and Polo models. title: History
content: From the Volkswagen idea to the Golf and the all-electric ID family; from the first foreign sales company in Canada to the founding of Volkswagen India; from Audi to Scania; from Wolfsburg to Chattanooga and Changchun: in German and English, the multimedia Chronicle provides a wide-ranging insight into the Volkswagen Group's history. The Corporate Archives in Wolfsburg provide the tools for this journey of discovery. It is the source of answers to questions on the history of Volkswagen, its products, plants and employees. ### Place of Remembrance of Forced Labour in the Volkswagen Factory. The “Place of Remembrance of Forced Labour in the Volkswagen Factory” is a permanent exhibition which opened in 1999. Volkswagen examines a wide range of aspects of its corporate history in numerous publications. For instance, the “Historical Notes” (Historische Notate – HN) series includes eye witness accounts of former forced labourers and publications on the post-war period as well as on various topics relating to the company’s history.

content: The company has shifted its focus toward electric vehicles, with plans to introduce multiple new electric models by 2026, aiming for 70% of its sales in Europe to be electric. Volkswagen AG, commonly known as Volkswagen or VW, is a prominent German automotive manufacturer headquartered in Wolfsburg, Lower Saxony. Founded on May 28, 1937, by the German Labour Front, the company was initially established to produce an affordable "people's car" as envisioned by Adolf Hitler. Over the decades, Volkswagen expanded its portfolio by acquiring various luxury brands, including Audi, Porsche, Bentley, and Lamborghini, which helped solidify its position as one of the largest automakers globally.
